In this context, we explore a privacy-preserving approach called federated learning that enables several entities to train a robust machine learning model jointly, without exchanging sensitive information. Based on how data is shared, FL can be classified into horizontal and vertical varieties. On one hand, hFL is examined where several entities have matching features and differing labels, while on the other hand, vFL is looked at, in which several entities have matching labels but vary in terms of features. One of the main contributions of this work is presenting a FL-based private query answer (FL-PPQA) protocol specifically suited for vertical data, which cooperates among several entities in the vFL setting without compromising their private data. To achieve this, we propose a new contribution that combines secure multi-party computation and homomorphic encryption techniques to ensure our proposed FL-PPQA is both secure and efficient. To demonstrate the validity of our approach, we conducted a set of experiments comparing our protocol with traditional secure multi-party computation methods and found that, in certain scenarios, our proposed FL-PPQA offers a more efficient and scalable solution. To do this, we utilized a real-world dataset from Kaggle.com and developed a Python-based framework to carry out a series of experiments, the results of which were carefully analyzed and presented to the research community.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet their scalability to large datasets is severely limited due to the computationally expensive nature of pairwise evaluations. In response, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on larger data sets. While widely adopted, this method has significant drawbacks, notably requiring an unnecessarily large number of features, directly proportional to the size of the dataset, in order to achieve satisfactory results comparable to traditional kernel-based methods. In order to circumvent these limitations and efficiently process large datasets, this paper introduces an alternative method of kernel approximation that leverages insights specific to the underlying data and offers both feature dimensionality reduction and performance enhancements. We test and evaluate this novel method against a range of competitors, including RFF, orthogonal random features, and the Nyström method.

In our study, we demonstrated how both a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner and a diagonal group are effectively incorporated into the wreath products under their combined, or product action, utilizing the Cartesian Decomposition technique.

This research paper examines conformally flat hypersurfaces of n-dimensional space (n is 4 or higher) within a hypersphere of n+2 dimensions. We start by classifying and describing these conformally flat hypersurfaces when they have constant M\"obius curvature under specific transformations. Next, we prove that a compact hypersurface with this constant M\"obius curvature, denoted L, is compact and can be represented as a compact form of a hypersurface with constant L\"obitt-Weyl curvature. The theorem also states that if this constant M\"obius curvature is not equal to (n-1)L, the hypersurface can be described as the union of a finite number of connected components, each of which can be mapped to a specific hypersurface \Sigma_{L}^{n} through a conformal transformation. If L is equal to (n-1)L, the hypersurface \tilde{\Sigma}_{L}^{n} consists of a finite number of connected components and has a finite total absolute M\"obius curvature.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created that maximizes energy gain and maintains a minimum data rate in a multi-user OFDMA network. Next, the model was refined to investigate throughput optimization in an SWIPT-enabled OFDMA system, resulting in a complex MINLP problem. Finally, an innovative harvesting technique based on a co-located receiver architecture and Generalized Antenna-Switching Technique was explored to improve the energy efficiency of SWIPT networks.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers often study network immunization, but traditional approaches typically focus on broad measures, such as network criticality and component size. In contrast, this paper delves into a micro-level analysis, where the removal of individual nodes during an attack is examined in detail. Based on percolation theory, the authors analyze the effects of removing a single node that causes other nodes to disconnect from the main component. Specifically, this paper investigates the number of nodes that become disconnected from the main component as a result of removing one node. By applying this micro-level approach to a random attack on a Cayley tree network, the distribution of the resulting node removal sizes is derived.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss in optical recycling systems. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. We present the concept of the sloshing Sagnac interferometer topology, an innovative variation of the Michelson design where the end mirrors are optically linked to form an additional resonating cavity. By transforming the detector into a system with multiple coupled cavities, this design outperforms the conventional single-cavity system and offers improved performance. By utilizing the sloshing design with multiple recycling mirrors of unequal frequencies, signal loss in the main detector is mitigated, thereby enhancing its sensitivity. A specific example using LIGO shows that this system can surpass the high-frequency sensitivity limit of current detectors without the use of signal sidebands or optical parametric amplifiers.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems are considered an exciting development, capable of providing rapid data transfer in crowded environments. As a result of their substantial size, MIMO arrays are subject to space-based disruptions and varying ranges that affect how data is perceived by nearby devices. With a high number of devices often present in applications for these systems and the scarcity of pilot signals available for them, designing protocols and scheduling methods is increasingly complex. To address this challenge, a new joint protocol has been developed that leverages varying reception areas of devices for better access and prioritizes scheduling of devices with distinct reception areas for more efficient signal sharing. According to the results obtained, this new scheme delivers considerable gains over traditional approaches in terms of overall connectivity, reduces data transfer delays, and significantly boosts the overall connectivity of the network.

Recent observations at sub-millimeter/millimeter wavelengths have revealed that the morphological structure of young stars' surrounding disks comprise various shapes, including symmetrical patterns and features resembling spiral arms, and localized curved formations. Prior research primarily focused on modeling planetary interactions in these disks to explain observed features, but this study suggests that turbulent flows could also be responsible for these structures. Using high-resolution, realistic simulations that account for gas dynamics, star-planet interactions, and potential sources of energy via turbulent patterns, this research demonstrates that the observed features can be attributed to turbulent flows without the necessity of forming rocks or clearing orbits. It is proposed that this mechanism leaves an extended signature that may eventually necessitate the inference of rock formation from the same patterns, and it is suggested that such features should be modeled to better understand far-infrared to millimeter wavelengths of telescopes like James Webb Space Telescope and ALMA's observations.

A question remains regarding the secondary component of GW190814 - whether it's a neutron star or a black hole of minimal mass. Researchers have introduced an effective mass, mu, combining the gravitational wave data from GW190814 and constraints from GW170817 to narrow down the equation of state parameter space. This equation state space can now be precisely located between 2.45-2.60 solar masses. If the neutron star hypothesis holds, this equation state space remains valid, but the secondary component's mass of 2.60 solar masses would be its last stable orbit mass.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency. We chose a frequency that maintains balanced two-axis cancellation forces to minimize negative impacts from strong Coulomb repulsion. Our method meets exact conditions for Gaussian amplitude and frequency modulation, allowing it to achieve high-order magnetic noise insensitivity without interference from center-of-mass mode couplings. Our analysis specifically targets recent experiments with Magneto-optical traps and provides an optimal frequency for setting lasers. We discovered that this arrangement allows the gate to maintain accuracy despite frequency mismatches up to $10^{6}$, a significant improvement over traditional methods that can only tolerate $10^{3}$, particularly beneficial for multi-ion quantum computing with spin sidesourcing protocols. Our research also includes suggested amplitude profiles for enhancing gate resilience.

Lately, researchers have been focusing on strong interactions in graphene's Dirac bands, which are composed of highly mobile electrons. However, strong interactions cannot be found in the electromagnetic spectrum alone, and strong correlations in graphene necessitate the use of localized states with higher angular momentum, like those in higher-dimensional systems with attached semimetallic layers. Consequently, this study explores and extends existing theories to explore multidimensional electron systems near the Dirac point, such as graphene on a d-dimensional lattice, and derives an inborn attraction in Coulomb potential when d is 4 or greater, leading to many-body bound states even after moving to 4d, and higher-dimensional systems near the Dirac point. A true composite particle is formed when it captures an excitation from the background, and in turn, leads to superconductivity in dimension 4 and above.

Researchers explored the capabilities of the NA62 experiment at CERN to enhance restrictions on a specific parameter in the Standard Model, specifically related to the interaction between a particular lepton and heavy neutral particles. By analyzing the process of $K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$, they determined the present limit can be set at $2\times 10^{-6}$ for a particular lepton interaction with masses ranging from 125 to 144 MeV, a region that current production searches lack in depth. Combining existing data with optimized detection tools or improved photon rejection techniques can significantly narrow this limit.

Neural language models have largely surpassed $N$-gram models due to better performance, but our findings suggest that $n$-gram models still excel in many scenarios with low computational costs, demonstrating a strong foundation for understanding language, despite the limitations of neural approaches. However, we found that combining $n$-gram models can significantly enhance predictive capabilities, surpassing previous methods that integrated $k$-best alternatives or formed an ensemble of multiple models. Our findings also reveal that backoff $n$-gram models with enhanced purity show substantial performance gains, but these benefits are most pronounced for larger values of $n$. Ultimately, our research aims to provide an alternative benchmark for language modeling and a baseline for future developments.

Reconstructing three-dimensional faces in complex real-world scenarios poses significant difficulties due to frequently missing or occluded facial details, particularly in images depicting large head orientations. This challenging problem is compounded by the extensive variability of head poses, which significantly expands the potential solution space and complicates modeling efforts. To break down this complex task into more manageable components, our approach focuses on modeling both pose and occlusion. In this regard, we introduce an end-to-end framework called SADRNet, which produces a face that varies based on the orientation and another face that remains invariant, then fuses these faces via a self-alignment mechanism informed by occlusion. Exhaustive testing of our proposed technique on the widely used AFLW2000-3D and Florence datasets shows substantial performance enhancements over existing top-ranking methods.

In an inflationary model, with a specific type of $\alpha$-attractor potential, we examine the behavior in the high-$k$ regime, where cosmological perturbations exhibit excessive growth and negative values of the Bardeen potential. This regime facilitates the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). Our calculations were carried out in a coordinate system adapted to the high-$k$ regime, transitioning to Compton coordinate during the collision of gravitational waves and matter overdensities at the horizon scale, to calculate the dark matter (DM) distribution resulting from PBH overproduction in the early universe. The resulting density profile resembles that obtained in the $\alpha$-attractor model with mild parameters, demonstrating the robustness of our approach in a wide range of regimes.

Researchers examined marked ordered trees with the ability to designate some right edges as "optional", given they don't lead to leaf nodes. They employed this model to analyze skew Dyck paths. A key aspect studied was the number of deepest nodes in these marked trees. Through explicit generating functions, they obtained insights, revealing the average number of deepest nodes converges to $\frac53$ as the number of nodes increases, which can be contrasted to standard ordered trees with a convergent average of $2$ deepest nodes.

This investigation seeks to examine the capabilities of Informed OCR (iOCR) in accurately capturing vote tabulation data, as the system is designed with an advanced spell-checking feature to correct common errors associated with traditional OCR technology, which the research reveals results in iOCR outperforming traditional OCR methods.

In recent years, significant progress has been made by the Amazonian company in developing advanced sorting algorithms for images, but this also highlights the limitations of existing theoretical frameworks by demonstrating that traditional data collection methods may be inefficient for independent data. As a result, there is a strong case to be made for the necessity of exploring exploratory reinforcement learning among peers. On the other hand, a reluctance to repeat profitable actions similar to a long-memory process is observed, which we investigate by developing a linear regression model with a decreasing coefficient in time and providing a theoretical analysis of its curiously high exploration risks that decline polynomially, in comparison to curiously high exploitation risks that decline polynomially. Both rate functions are also illustrated with non-increasing examples with power and exponential laws. A fractional Gaussian process is additionally provided as a high-resolution demonstration of our model. Both the optimal tuning of parameters and post-hoc optimization of parameters are also examined with our analysis.

A key factor for maintaining stability in future low-carbon power grids is expected to be energy storage systems. Studies examining past experiences reveal a common issue with storage units - they frequently fail to take advantage of high-price signals during periods of low energy supply. This behavior has been often attributed to inaccurate forecasting or operational issues. However, our research suggests a more plausible explanation, rooted in the risk-averse nature of most market participants. Utilizing actual data from the 24-hour Australian electricity market, our research develops and tests a game-theoretic model that incorporates risk preferences. Contrary to prior studies observing under-utilization, our findings show that a risk-averse attitude actually promotes effective utilization of storage resources.

A simplified computer model is used to investigate various global atmospheric circulation patterns in an Earth-like atmosphere by simulating and experimenting with different rotation rates and temperature differences between the equator and the poles. To better understand these experiments, various factors such as the Coriolis effect, atmospheric stability, and tropical convection are taken into consideration with the help of basic fluid dynamics principles. By analyzing and comparing the results of the simulations, trends in how heat is distributed around the globe and in higher latitudes are identified and discussed, and a detailed account of the simulations is provided for a range of simulations with different rotation rates and temperature differences from the equator to the poles.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) benefit from being trained on optimal subsets of annotated data. Active learning algorithms excel in this area, yet their application is hindered due to the necessity of extensive data labeling. To address this limitation, we introduced a novel ALS (Active Learning with Self-supervised pretraining) method. This innovative approach leverages the power of self-supervised pretraining, reducing the need for full data annotation. The ALS method's framework was validated with the cyclic label propagation technique, and its efficacy was demonstrated through experiments on the CIFAR10 and STAMP datasets, showcasing an 11% improvement over the standard AL selection criterion.

Researchers who utilize silicon donor spin have reached a record for coherence time using a single donor. However, to achieve an order of magnitude faster gate speeds and to develop a network of connected nodes, researchers must comprehend and manipulate the behavior of systems with multiple donors. The accuracy of existing models that predict electron density and spin interaction strengths falls short, particularly when dealing with smaller donor distances. Utilizing a combination of experimental data and simulations, this study presents a model that more precisely captures how electrons behave, accounting for their tendency to redistribute when spins interact. This model offers a significant improvement in predicting spin interactions, even in closer-range donor settings, and reveals a striking relationship between spin interactions and electron density. This model also provides a detailed understanding of electron density patterns, which is essential for using optical methods to manipulate optical-nuclear spins around a single donor, as is discussed in the accompanying Supplementary Information.

Our investigation focused on the transport properties of HgTe quantum wells near their critical thickness, where the energy gap is minimal, and the energy spectrum is described by a singular Dirac cone structure. Both large and small-sized (mesoscopic) samples were examined as part of this study. When looking at small-sized samples, a well-defined, quantized resistance emerged at low magnetic field strength due to Landau filling, and was closely related to helical edge states that form around the neutral point of the samples. Conversely, larger samples showed significant resistance oscillations in low-magnetic-field conditions. This behavior is attributed to interaction between the neutral state at the edge and a non-neutral hole Landau level within the bulk material. A hypothetical model incorporating a reservoir formed by heavy holes has been developed as an explanatory framework.

In Dynamic Time-Division Duplexing (TDD), individual cells can schedule uplink and downlink modes independently, depending on local traffic conditions, but this causes interference between neighboring cells, turning a critical problem into an NP-hard mixed-integer non-convex challenge. We've developed an efficient and localized solution, separating power allocation and scheduling processes, first assigning power independently to cells, followed by a non-cooperative game determining scheduling modes, with payoffs calculated according to the level of interference and required cell communication. Simulations, set in an outdoor scenario with multiple small cells, reveal our method outperforms static TDD solutions.

In this work, we introduce a novel meta-learning framework centered on ODE neural networks, which acquires an understanding of gradients. This framework grants optimizers enhanced flexibility by leveraging the properties of Neural ODEs, as long as they satisfy the condition needed to recover the essential dynamics of a system from input-output data. Our research presents several distinct metalearners that utilize this gradient prior, which we analyze both theoretically and through extensive empirical testing. These models demonstrate superior performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods, while also offering benefits such as faster training, increased accuracy, and the ability to handle larger datasets. Our visualizations of learned representations and gradients provide valuable insights into the representational efficiency of our models as well as the unique capabilities of our framework, which can accommodate non-differentiable components, handle scenarios with limited data, and manage larger problem scales.

Simply enhancing a machine learning model's accuracy is not sufficient, as we must also focus on increasing its reliability. This consideration is crucial for creating robust AI systems with the capacity to safely handle critical applications like self-driving technology. We propose an innovative multi-objective optimization framework known as SATLearn, specifically designed to improve both the accuracy and trustworthiness of binary classification models while ensuring compliance with safety constraints. We assess SATLearn using real-world data sets and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving enhanced accuracy and reliability, effectively balancing these two objectives and adhering to predefined safety parameters. Furthermore, we examine SATLearn in various scenarios, including scenarios where accuracy and reliability are prioritized, within their feasible ranges.

A newly defined polynomial, referred to as the nth toroidal colored Jones polynomial, is established for links in a thickened torus. Dubbed $J_n^T$, this polynomial demonstrates numerous properties similar to the original colored Jones polynomial, and notably displays volume conjecture behavior. By applying $J_n^T$, we prove the volume conjecture holds true for a specific link, and provide computational data suggesting it holds for additional links. Moreover, $J_n^T$ can be represented through two distinct constructions, a pseudo-operator invariant, and a construction rooted in the Kauffman bracket skein module of the torus. Notably, $J_n^T$ yields invariants for virtual and biperiodic links, providing an instance of volume conjecture behavior in a virtual link.

The primary objective of Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) involves determining the appropriate sense of a word with multiple meanings within a particular context.  Advances in deep learning, specifically utilizing BERT, have led to significant progress in this area, with several strategies being developed to combine structured knowledge for enhanced performance.  Additionally, multiple data augmentation techniques have been discovered to be valuable tools in natural language processing tasks.  Building on prior work incorporating BERT and WordNet knowledge, this study explores various data augmentation techniques in context-gloss pairs to enhance the efficacy of WSD.  Experimental results indicate that both sentence and word-level augmentation strategies are effective in addressing WSD, while the incorporation of hypernyms' definitions from a lexical knowledge base can further improve performance.  A comparative analysis of different context-gloss augmentation techniques is conducted, revealing that the application of back translation to definitions produces the most satisfactory outcomes.

This study formulates a genuine integral expression of the reciprocal gamma function in terms of a modified hypersingular integral. It also proves the connection to the traditional complex representation, in addition to obtaining a modified complex representation following the standard Hankel path.

The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC detected the production of top quarks for the first time using proton-lead data at an 8.16 TeV nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy. Top quark production was identified in events featuring one isolated electron or muon and four or more jets, from a data set totaling 174 inverse nanobarns of luminosity. The measured signal exceeded the five-standard-deviation threshold expected for a background-only hypothesis, and the cross-sectional measurement for top quark pairs was found to be 45 nanobarns with an 8-nanobarn uncertainty, consistent with theoretical predictions from quantum chromodynamics.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed framework over baseline models in terms of execution and exact set match accuracy when database contents are inaccessible, with further analysis pointing to areas for future improvement.

This paper delves into the utilization of differential privacy within the framework of graph-based data. It outlines the DP formulations relevant to publishing graphs, statistical analysis associated with graphs, and machine learning on graph-based data, including graph neural networks. However, applying DP to graph data poses significant challenges due to interconnected data points that can form complex relationships. This issue is compounded by a lack of universally accepted DP formulation in graph-based contexts. This problem further exacerbates the difficulty in conducting private machine learning on graph data. A notable absence of systematized research on graph-based learning in relation to privacy was a key driver for this work, which is to explore and compare various formulation of graph-based learning from a privacy perspective. By examining diverse graph neural network training methods, we highlight different privacy perspectives, including core differential privacy notions, graph usage, and graph size. Furthermore, we touch upon theoretical results on privacy costs in graph-based learning. This work is intended to provide the research community with a clear understanding of the graph-based learning formulation in relation to privacy, along with key insights on possible paths forward.

The vast amount of images, data, and resources that Euclid will generate positions the consortium to create comprehensive legacy databases of outstanding quality, encompassing high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy with significant implications for the study of galaxies. These proceedings outline the promising opportunities and scientific breakthroughs Euclid will achieve in the areas of galaxy and AGN development, the evolution of the cosmos, investigations of the Milky Way, and various other celestial bodies and phenomena.

Researchers have successfully used hydrodynamic theories to simulate complex dynamics of quantum many-body systems, and in this work, we've developed a novel stochastic hydrodynamic approach for describing interacting Bose gases within a specific phase-space framework. This new hybrid method combines the advantages of a hydrodynamic description and enables Monte Carlo simulations, allowing us to track the time evolution of the dense quantum system while maintaining the reversible nature of particle collisions through the use of phase-space flipping. Furthermore, the formulation allows for the application of efficient particle-mesh simulations, enabling us to implement short-range interaction operators effectively. As in our study, we've focused on describing the time evolution of a two-dimensional interacting Bose gas in a presence of a vortex defect, and has been possible to implement long-range Coulomb interactions via a precise simulation of the associated electrostatic potential. The resulting numerical simulations, which involve $N=400$ particles, have yielded a high-resolution simulation of the system's dynamics, offering a level of detail previously unattainable with other stochastic hydrodynamic formulations. This new approach, which we've presented, provides a valuable intermediate level of approximation for understanding the system's behavior in the transition between the ballistic and hydrodynamic regimes, and has also opened up possibilities for simulating few-particle corrections to fluid dynamics via reweighting techniques.

Given an independent and identically distributed sequence of letters broken down into words based on independent and identically distributed renewal times, an independent and identically distributed sequence of words is formed.  The annealed large deviation principle (LDP) for the empirical process of words is characterized by a rate function that equals the specific relative entropy of the observed distribution of words with respect to the reference distribution of words.  For renewal times with an algebraic tail, a quenched LDP (conditioned on a typical sequence of letters) was established by Birkner, Gantert, and Shu (2014), which was shown to have a rate function equal to the specific relative entropy of the observed distribution of letters with respect to the marginal distribution of the reference sequence of letters, conditioned on producing a typical number of letters.  It is shown that when the reference sequence of words has an exponential tail, the rate function of the quenched LDP equals the specific relative entropy of the observed distribution of letters with respect to the marginal distribution of the reference sequence of letters, and that the condition of the independent and identically distributed sequence of words is superfluous in this context.  However, when the reference sequence of words is only conditionally independent given the total number of letters, and that number follows a heavy-tailed distribution, the rate function of the quenched LDP is equal to the specific relative entropy of the observed distribution of letters with respect to the marginal distribution of the reference sequence

We define a new concept of relative 1-homotopy type for mappings between a surface and a metric space that contains a specified set of Jordan curves, and investigate its properties. This enables us to prove the existence and local smoothness of the surfaces with minimal area within a particular 1-homotopy type when embedded in a surface with non-negative curvature. Additionally, we establish that when the ambient surface has positive curvature, these surfaces enjoy a stronger form of smoothness, namely they are globally smooth. This in turn allows us to establish a version of a theorem by Gromov and Schoen regarding the solvability of the $\bar{g}$-energy equation in settings with strictly convex surfaces.

Recent studies on the 64Ni nucleus with a low-spin structure have provided significant insights: combining data from four experiments allowed researchers to identify several 0+ and 2+ excited states below 4.5 MeV, and characterize their properties. Using a Monte Carlo shell model, scientists were able to explain the findings and uncover a surprisingly intricate pattern of shapes existing together, where a high-energy prolate 0+ state was identified.

Machine learning models often undergo performance assessment through k-fold cross-validation to facilitate model selection and parameter adjustment. Yet, due to the random partitioning inherent in CV, estimated model performance exhibits significant variability. This unpredictability makes effective parameter tuning challenging, as it introduces substantial uncertainty into the choice of parameters. Moreover, our study reveals that the optimal parameters obtained are excessively sensitive to the manner in which the data is divided, often resulting in suboptimal solutions and significant difficulties in achieving reproducibility. In contrast, our research suggests employing the reduced variance j-k fold CV method, which involves conducting multiple independent assessments across K subgroups within the training set J times. In place of the conventional single random partition, the best parameters are chosen based on aggregated performance outcomes. The novelty of this approach is highlighted by its incorporation into the scikit-learn Python library. Our study demonstrates the benefits of using large values for both K and J, particularly when applied to high-dimensional data in NLP, shows that this method successfully delivers consistent results for various baselines and facilitates the discovery of 7% more accurate configurations compared to the conventional K-fold CV method.

Deep Neural Networks with vast parameters have faced challenges in real-time deployment, prompting the utilization of Teacher-Student architectures to distill knowledge from large Teacher networks into efficient Student networks. Initially utilized in CAMA and Reversible Neural Networks knowledge learning, these architectures excel in maintaining performance while preserving the Teacher network's structure. This innovation was innovated upon by Zhang et al.'s work on S4-Teacher architecture, which combines Multi-Scale Attention and SE modules, achieving accurate knowledge transmission with camse blocks as the Student's foundation. In this work, we integrate SE modules with camse blocks to create an enhanced Teacher-Student architecture, called S4ST, where the Teacher incorporates full attention and residual pathways, and a refined Student with single-head attention and channel refinement modules. In our approach, the Teacher network's comprehensive information is transmitted to the Student, who learns from it using a single-head attention mechanism and channel residual pathways for enhanced representation. Our results across multiple datasets, including TWR, demonstrate the efficacy of the S4ST architecture, achieving 47.5 MB memory usage and a MAC of 2.06 GFLOPs while outperforming prior models such as MobileNetV4 and Bird's camse based architecture in both accuracy and efficiency.

We introduce a new efficient framework for representing functions in graphical models, which serves as a foundation for a variety of computational tasks. Our concise model then leverages this framework, specifically using deterministic finite state automata within a variable elimination approach known as Bucket Elimination. We dub this variant FABE, which we found significantly enhances Bucket Elimination by substantially reducing the computational time and memory usage. Our FABE approach compares favourably to the current state of the art methods, particularly recursive best-first and structured message passing for the most probable explanation, as well as CPLEX, GUROBI, and toulbar2 for constrained optimization. These improvements are demonstrated with a wide range of problems across different models, showing that FABE can reduce the computational time and memory for the most probable explanation by up to four orders of magnitude in our experiments.

We investigated the absorption of a single, monochromatic light beam at 689 nm as it passes through a cloud of ultracold $^{88}$Sr atoms. Due to the interaction, the absorption pattern deviates significantly, taking on an asymmetric shape as a result of a shift in frequency that is equivalent in magnitude to the natural width of a specific atomic transition in strontium. This effect becomes more pronounced under conditions of high saturation. Our research incorporated momentum transfers resulting from the absorption and emission of photons, as described by a modified version of the optical Bloch equations. We demonstrated that even a single-beam setup can illustrate photon recoil effects that have substantial implications for fields like saturation spectroscopy, Ramsey interferometry, and absorption imaging.

When subjected to high stresses, the vast majority of dense mixtures undergo a sudden and extreme thickening, characterized by a transition from fluid-like behavior to rigidity. Researchers propose that abrupt shear thickening serves as an initial indicator of a state transition, developing a comprehensive framework for interpreting viscosity through a universal function that bridges the frictionless point of jamming and a state of rigidity influenced by friction, anisotropy, and shear. Studies involving cornstarch in glycerol and silica spheres in glycerol found that for these two systems, viscosity can be condensed into a singular, stress- and volume fraction-independent curve, revealing distinct scaling regimes that reflect different universality classes and implying that isotropic and anisotropic shear jamming have unique characteristics. Furthermore, by integrating the effects of microscale interactions into a dimensionless variable that gauges the distance from the shear jamming transition, scientists have laid the groundwork for connecting the principles of universal physics with material-specific properties.

Recently introduced is a higher rank algebra known as the Racah algebra $R(n)$. A special variant, termed the special Racah algebra $sR(n)$, is then defined as a quotient of the Racah algebra by its central elements. It is then demonstrated that this $sR(n)$ algebra corresponds to a specific quotient of a certain centralizer $Z(n)$ located in the universal enveloping algebra of $U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, with the mapping proven for sufficiently large values of 2λ. Additionally, a method is developed to characterize the ideals in $Z(n)$, which are responsible for the formation of the Racah algebra(s).

An area of public information science is Web search personalisation, where algorithms are used to tailor individual Web search results based on various parameters. The significance of Web search without personalisation is examined in this examination, where an alternative argument is presented that it is a fundamental tool that provides broad overview of general information on the World Wide Web. The case for Web search without personalisation as a standard is further strengthened by quantitative analysis of the amount of information omitted, which was found to be nearly 99% of the data. The drastic disparity between general and personalised Web search is also discussed along with the implications of these findings and possible alternative perspectives.

We are suggesting the establishment of a state-of-the-art muon-proton and muon-nucleus collider that operates at the TeV level, capable of delivering highly accurate measurements in deep inelastic scattering in new areas, while also offering a comprehensive research agenda in particle and nuclear physics. By doing so, we believe it could either drive the advancement or make use of existing particle accelerators, specifically taking advantage of established infrastructure if constructed at places like Brookhaven National Laboratory, Fermilab, or CERN. In this concept, we outline various design parameters for several collider configurations and evaluate potential for scientific discoveries with studies on deep inelastic scattering processes, Higgs boson and vector boson production, top quark creation, and leptoquark beyond Standard Model. Additionally, considerations for detector designs and potential paths to realization are also discussed.

A significant challenge in employing DWI and PCI MRI techniques for the assessment and monitoring of brain tumors is motion caused by respiration. To mitigate this issue, a real-time motion-compensated imaging method based on GRAPPA PCI was developed. This approach achieves accurate compensation for head motion and respiratory-induced shifts. The method involves multiple steps: first, reference networks for both DWI and PCI data are created to replace missing signal values. Then, a set of linear models is used to capture the relationship between motion parameters and image intensity, separately for each voxel. These models are established using PCI data with high spatial resolution. Missing signal values in the DWI dataset are filled using the derived relations. Finally, DWI data are combined through multiplication to obtain a motion-corrected dataset. Experimentation was carried out using phantom data as well as images obtained from four healthy volunteers. Results showed that this method restores displaced signal values and produces a DWI image that is free from motion artifacts. When compared to manual cropping, the set of linear models demonstrated an improved capacity to account for signal displacement. This method provides a precise and efficient solution for motion correction in brain imaging.

The paired-permutation test in NLP systems has long relied on testing the statistical significance of differences in performance. This test aims to verify that observed discrepancies aren't simply coincidental. Despite the importance of accurate results, a lack of suitable exact algorithms forces practitioners to use time-consuming Monte Carlo approximations to achieve this goal. In contrast, we've developed an efficient method for calculating paired-permutation test results exactly. This exact algorithm takes significantly less time to compute than Monte Carlo methods. In particular, we observed a 10 times speedup when using our exact algorithm versus the commonly employed Monte Carlo approximation on a representative dataset of 20000 samples.

A comprehensive dataset of freight rates, shipping quantities, new ship prices, used ship prices, and scrapped ship prices has been assembled from 1970 to 2009. Furthermore, pricing information for containers, modified shipping rates, and corresponding export and import quantities for various goods has been incorporated. A structural econometric model was developed to explain historical data using the assembled datasets and past research findings. The study also explores the effects of environmental policies on the shipping industry and rates. The effects policy interventions have on the market and their observable impacts have been examined through counterfactual analyses.

We define loom spaces as a more general framework incorporating leaf spaces for pseudo-Anosov flows and link spaces for veering triangulations. Building on Gu\'eritaud's research, it is demonstrated that there is a veering triangulation inherently linked to every loom space, with this correspondence maintaining a deformation invariance property that aligns with the loom space of a veering triangulation to that of the flow obtained by veering triangulation subdivision. Additionally, if a manifold has a loom space, it is confirmed that the manifold is hyperbolic.

The recent interest in the stock market can be attributed to substantial fluctuations in the US stock index during March 2020, highlighting the significance of news and social media in affecting stock prices. To analyze this impact, a sentiment dataset was created by extracting headlines from Reuters, Associated Press, and Bloomberg related to the US stock market from April 2019 to February 2020, which were then manually categorized into positive, negative, and neutral categories. A neural network-based classifier was employed to create a large-scale dataset, and the resulting labeled data was refined using the Active Learning process. This dataset was utilized to conduct an event study on the S&P 500, revealing that days with predominantly positive or negative news headlines led to subsequent days' stock market reactions. Notably, days with neutral news headlines had no such effect.

This research investigates double Higgs boson production at future electron-positron colliders CLIC and ILC with TeV-scale energies within the framework of Effective Field Theories, interpreting new parameters from new physics as independent fields. Initially, we establish that at these high energies, the longitudinal component in the electron beam contributes roughly 60% to the total cross-section for this process. Next, we compute the effective field theory Lagrangian incorporating the Higgs Effective Field Theory and a dimension-8 operator known as $C_{HB}$. We find that including $C_{HB}$ in calculations results in a significant (16%-22%) enhancement of the expected signal yields for new searches at these colliders. We then compare the predicted signals for this process in the full and effective field theories and find that, given the anticipated sensitivities of these colliders to $c_{HW}$ and $c_{HWB}$ coefficients (around 1%-3%), they would also be capable of probing combinations of higher-dimensional operator coefficients, specifically $C_{HB}$ and mixes of $C_{H}$, $C_{H}$, and $C_{HW}$ to levels of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-5}$, providing a valuable tool for probing new physics through vector boson fusion processes in the Higgs boson pair search.

We perform a covariant expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action in powers of
$1/c^2$, considering a generic spacetime foliation defined by $c$, the speed
of light. We achieve this through the application of a suitable 'pre-non-
relativistic' geometrical parametrization, thereby facilitating an
analytical $1/c^2$ expansion of general relativity. Ultimately, this method
permits an in-depth examination of the Einstein-Hilbert action expansion up to
its next-to-next-to-leading order.

We investigated the drag experienced by a long cylindrical solid moving through a layer of granular material, specifically polysterene and hydrogel grains, at various speeds and depths. The cylinder was oriented both perpendicular and parallel to its long axis as it moved, and we found that the drag it experienced differed significantly in the two orientations, a phenomenon we call anisotropy. This anisotropy varied greatly with the speed at which the cylinder was moved, its length compared to its width, and whether the grains it was moving through had high friction or little friction. Notably, the anisotropy increased more quickly in beds with low friction. Additionally, the drag experienced by the cylinder was found to be influenced more by its long axis than its ends. This phenomenon could be understood by studying the flow of sediment around the cylinder and estimating the drag experienced by its sides and flat ends.

Our research examined the connection between initial anisotropic geometry and anisotropic flow within a multiphase transport model, specifically for 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions. Contrary to elliptical flow's dependence on centrality, we discovered minimal variation in triangular flow centrality. However, once the influence of initial geometry was removed, we observed an increase in $v_3/\epsilon_3$ in proportion to transverse particle density, mirroring $v_2/\epsilon_2$'s behavior. Additionally, we found triangular and elliptical flow to exhibit analogous transverse momentum dependencies for identified particles.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing evaluations of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and the determination of CP-violating processes in $B^0_s \to J/\psi\phi$.

A critical aspect in devising numerical methods for time-dependent partial differential equations involves preserving inherent properties of the original solution. Researchers have a rich history of developing and analyzing preservation-based discretization techniques, including validating existing schemes's preservation properties and proposing innovative methods achieving both high accuracy and property preservation. Although such schemes often require ensuring certain conditions on the mesh, many previously proposed methods failed to meet this requirement, including a 2014 proposal for a high-order scheme. This dissertation proposes new high-order numerical methods that satisfy inherent constraints, are second and higher order accurate, and meet necessary conditions on the mesh, with a focus on preserving positivity for a class of partial differential equations.

Soft-tissue navigation is highly dependent on non-rigid registration. For laparoscopic liver surgery, we integrate an organ model with intraoperative ultrasound by analyzing the relationship between ultrasound and model features. Existing methods for enhancing registration accuracy have focused on deforming the organ model; an alternative approach is to deform the ultrasound itself. In this work, we re-examine the problem with a new perspective: interpreting ultrasound as an image intensity distribution that undergoes spatial and scale transformations, along with local intensity adjustments to better align with the organ model. We propose a new method, known as LiverFit, utilizing a deep generative model called Normalizing Flow to perform non-rigid organ deformation. Numerical simulations and practical applications of LiverFit are also presented and discussed.

Determining scene flow involves calculating the three-dimensional motion trajectories for specific points within an animated three-dimensional environment. Motion trajectory data has been found beneficial for downstream tasks, including depth mapping, optical flow, and control. Utilizing data-driven models for flow estimation has led to significant advancements, albeit with limitations in handling sparse observations and a lack of generalizability. Our proposed approach, a novel neural network architecture called DYS (Dynamic Scene Network), has rectified these issues by utilizing a long-term memory module, a myopic predictor, and a control task module. Our network is capable of handling sparse observations, while also具有一年期的能力 to replicate and controlling animated scenes through control task module. Experimental outcomes on both real and simulated datasets, including the KMAR dataset, demonstrate the DYS's superior performance in estimating motion vectors, controlling the scenes, and a comparison with existing neural network architectures, such as the RNM.

In recent years, AI networks, specifically those based on artificial neural systems, have significantly outperformed competitors in a wide range of tasks including image recognition, sound analysis, and language interpretation. However, widespread use of such models was previously hindered due to their massive computational requirements for both initial training and operational deployment. Neuromorphic computing technology, which allows bio-realistic neural networks to operate at high speeds while minimizing energy consumption, has now become an appealing substitute. We present a proposal to utilize a Random Neural Network as a versatile classifying model that combines the efficiency of spiking neural networks with the high classification accuracy achieved by traditional neural networks, showcasing this concept's effectiveness across real-world classification datasets.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the context of the bag model, and also examined the impact of the temperature and magnetic field on the properties of spin-polarized strange quark matter.

A Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property in a graph implies that each perfect matching can be combined with another to create a Hamiltonian cycle. This concept was first introduced by A. A. Kelmans and I. V. Areshchek in 2010 under the name $\mathcal{R}$-cycles. 

A theorem by J. Bang-Jensen et al. in 2 directed graphs and hamiltonian cycles establishes that for any 2-directed graph satisfying the conditions of the PMH-property, it holds for all subgraphs as well. 

We will build on this research by providing a method to decompose an arbitrary 2-directed graph into components, some of which are subgraph-PMH-property-reducing, and others that maintain the PMH-property. 

Additionally, we will describe an $\mathcal{R}$-cycle decomposition process, breaking down cycles into shorter cycles by vertex edges, and providing computer assistance to identify specific structures that 2-directed graphs must possess.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call filtering policies in containerized applications. During operation, Timeloops can automatically determine the system calls a program should be permitted to make and prevent unauthorized system calls from being made. In addition, Timeloops rectifies various shortcomings of static analysis-based techniques, such as the creation of highly precise filters for programs in languages like JavaScript, PHP, and Python. Developed using standard, reliable technologies, Timeloops features a simple and efficient design comprising less than 500 lines of code. Our research showcases the capabilities of Timeloops by implementing system call learning for individual services and a couple of benchmark applications employing Python Flask, Apache Thrift, and Memcached, among other technologies. Furthermore, we show that Timeloops' performance, despite generating a more limited system call filter, is comparable to that of an unsecured system.

This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target appearance probabilities are organized on a grid. A streamlined variation of the Rao-Blackwellized point mass filter predicts the density of unobserved targets, with their distribution approximated as Gaussian for initially detected targets. Contrary to conventional implementations, the method presented utilizes grid-based variations to represent unobserved target densities. As a result, sharp boundaries can be created around areas within the region of interest that fall outside of a sensor's field of view, which has significant advantages over conventional Gaussian mixture models (which are based on multiple unnormalized Gaussian distributions) in their ability to track the number of detected targets over time and smooth out variations in their data. A full algorithm is provided for the predicted unobserved target densities in the region of interest, including the implementation of grid-based variations, which can be efficiently computed using grid convolution methods and exhibit superior performance in terms of computational efficiency. Furthermore, the predicted detection probabilities of unobserved targets in the region of interest are shown to be comparable in their performance to the variation of the point mass filter (RPF-PPM) in their ability to track the number of targets over time, with enhanced smoothness in the results obtained.

This study examines the null controllability of a population model that includes an interior degenerate diffusion component. By first establishing a new Carleman estimate for the adjoint system in its entirety, and subsequently deriving a relevant observability inequality, we aim to demonstrate the existence of a localized control action capable of driving the population towards extinction within a finite time frame.

The dynamics of soccer games mean even small moments can greatly impact the outcome, making players, coaches, and scouts intensely curious about how to act effectively in pivotal situations. In such moments, teams often lose possession of the ball and may end up playing with a one-goal advantage. To assist in making informed decisions during these high-stakes scenarios, we developed a policy that helps choose between attacking with a one-goal lead or conserving the lead by playing for a goalless draw. We built an extensive dataset of real games, allowing us to analyze how factors like time remaining, goal difference, and positioning influence the best course of action. We used this data to training reinforcement learning models, comparing them to policy based on ordinary points. We found the new approach yielded a policy that maximizes the probability of winning, one-goal margin, and overall point margin by one. We demonstrated this policy in simulations and live matches, measuring success based on expected goal difference. It also led to a new way to quantify uncertainty in in-play betting, accounting for fluctuations in goal difference.

High-resolution subsurface modeling via seismic imaging has the potential to be greatly improved with Full Waveform Inversion (FWI).  However, FWI can become trapped in local minima due to its nonlinear optimization nature. Two alternative methods, Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (WRI) and Extended Source Waveform Inversion (ESI), have been proposed to provide broader convergence for the desired Earth model. Although WRI and ESI offer superior convergence, they also introduce excessive computation from redundant source signals in the forward modeling process. A new efficiency-enhancing approach, spatial-sparse ESI (SS-ESI), is now presented to address this issue by selectively activating source receivers in the data acquisition system for FWI/WRI and ESI. SS-ESI achieves the desired cost reduction by utilizing collapsed cross-correlation to represent the integrated wavefields from source signals, as opposed to individual wavefields from each. A proof-of-concept example using 2D synthetic data is provided to illustrate the desired cost reduction of SS-ESI compared to ESI.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetrical noisy voter model was developed for a regular lattice structure. The model allows one species to colonize nearest-neighbor sites, while another species can settle at any distance but is less successful in doing so. The model includes external noise, which can lead to random species swaps in the lattice. The combination of these dynamics results in various species competition outcomes, including the exclusion of one species, distinct population coexistence, or bistable coexistence dependent on the starting population ratio. The model shows that an abrupt transition occurs as immigration intensity surpasses a critical point, causing the irreversible decline of the species with shorter dispersal range due to a cusp catastrophe leading to half loop dynamics.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. This hybrid network allows a central hub to transfer data to those in need and supply power to those who require it. This coexistence also allows D2D transmissions to use the same spectrum. This integrated network is divided into two halves, with the first half transmitting D2D data and the second half receiving it. This split is necessary to prevent the lack of an transmitter in the second half from being an issue. This integrated network is also equipped with an intelligent reflecting surface, which is used to improve the efficiency of data and energy transmissions while not using any additional power. This surface has one or more elements that can reflect signals, with each element being used to control the phase and amplitude of the reflected signals.
